question: How does a single artificial neuron compute its output?

storyboard.learning_goal: Understand that a single artificial neuron computes y = activation( sum(w_i * x_i) + b ) and trace that computation with concrete numbers including a negative weight and bias shift.
storyboard.driving_question: How does a single artificial neuron turn numbers in into a number out?
storyboard.learner_start: Knows multiplication and addition; has seen flow diagrams but not the neuron formula or what weights, bias and activation do.
storyboard.representation: Chosen method: 3Blue1Brown-style worked derivation combined with mechanism trace. Why it fits: the learning difficulty is why scaling then shifting then reshaping yields the output; changing geometry and numeric readouts substantiates each algebraic step rather than stating the formula. TextMode is labels beside geometry plus short numeric readouts; full definitions stay visible so the infographic teaches without audio. Capability gap: renderer limited to circle, box, text, arrow, line, path, svg, so neuron body is circle, weights are arrows with text values, activation is a path plot, no rich neural rendering needed.
assumptions: ReLU used as concrete activation; same weighted-sum plus bias structure holds for other activations
Example values are illustrative, not learned from data

visual_design.why: Mechanism flow left-to-right exposes order inputs->scale->sum->shift->reshape, while quantitative text readouts expose how values transform; neither alone shows why output is 0.7
visual_design.misreading: Viewer might think larger visual size means larger importance, or that arrows imply inputs physically move, or that activation curve height is the output value
visual_design.safeguard: Every object keeps its numeric text value; sign is stated in words and as + / - text, not by styling alone; sum and output are separate text readouts beside the curve with a marker dot showing mapping
encodings: text numbers beside objects mean current values
arrow connection means multiply-and-carry from input to sum
path kink means activation rule mapping sum to output
sign text + / - with words positive / negative means weight direction

beats.question: What does a single neuron actually receive?
beats.insight: A neuron receives several distinct numbers at once that stay identifiable before any math.
beats.change: Two input_token circles enter on left labeled 1.0 and 0.5; context circle for neuron body appears in center with output stub to right
beats.after: Viewer sees two separate inputs aimed at one common container, no computation yet
beats.reasoning: Visible separation before transformation establishes inputs as independent trackable cases carried through later beats
beats.camera: Static wide on left inputs and central container to establish flow order
beats.narration: A neuron [cue:b1_show_inputs]receives several numbers at once. Here [cue:b1_track_example]we will follow two inputs, 1.0 and 0.5, into one neuron body.
beats.visual_test: With sound off learner can point to each input circle and state its value and that no combination has happened yet

beats.question: How does the neuron treat inputs unequally?
beats.insight: Each input is scaled by its own weight, including a negative sign, then added into a single total.
beats.before: Two input values and central container visible
beats.change: attention_weight arrows appear between inputs and center labeled with weights; embedding_vector boxes show products 0.8 and minus 0.2; they merge into result readout for the weighted sum without bias
beats.after: Viewer sees 1.0 scaled to 0.8 and 0.5 scaled to minus 0.2, converging to one intermediate total of 0.6
beats.reasoning: Seeing the same inputs transform to products then to one sum makes scaling-then-adding visible as distinct from just adding inputs
beats.camera: Focus on weight arrows and product boxes, then shift to sum junction to show many-to-one convergence
beats.narration: Each connection [cue:b2_show_weights]scales its input by a weight. The first weight is positive, [cue:b2_show_products]so 1.0 becomes 0.8, while the second weight has sign = - , so 0.5 becomes minus 0.2, and [cue:b2_show_sum]they add to a single total.
beats.visual_test: Learner can compute each product from visible numbers and explain why one contribution subtracts because its sign is negative

beats.question: Why add a bias and apply an activation?
beats.insight: Bias shifts the total, activation reshapes it; the final output is the reshaped shifted sum, not the raw sum.
beats.before: Weighted sum of 0.6 visible at center
beats.change: part box with +0.1 joins result to make z=0.7; probability_dist ReLU path appears to the right with marker dot at 0.7; sampled_output box appears showing y=0.7
beats.after: Viewer sees sum shift from 0.6 to 0.7 then map through kinked function to output 0.7
beats.reasoning: Adding a new term to the existing total then passing the same value through a plotted function shows shift and reshape as two separate operations on the same trackable number
beats.camera: Hold sum in view while revealing bias join, then pan right to activation plot and output
beats.narration: Next [cue:b3_add_bias]a bias of plus 0.1 shifts the total from 0.6 to 0.7. Then [cue:b3_show_curve]the activation reshapes that number, and [cue:b3_show_output]the output appears as 0.7 because ReLU leaves positive values unchanged.
beats.visual_test: Learner can state the shifted value and, given the plotted rule, predict output for a negative shifted sum would be zero

beats.question: Can we trace the whole computation end-to-end?
beats.insight: Output 0.7 follows directly from (0.8*1.0 + -0.4*0.5 + 0.1) passed through ReLU; changing any term changes the result predictably.
beats.change: Sequential highlight pulse runs left-to-right recomputing 0.8, minus 0.2, 0.6, 0.7, 0.7 while equation text builds below
beats.after: Viewer sees complete formula y=ReLU(0.8*1.0 + -0.4*0.5 + 0.1)=0.7 with each term linked to its object
beats.reasoning: Replaying the same example as one continuous transformation connects prior separate insights into a usable model the learner can rerun
beats.camera: Static wide to keep entire chain in view during replay for comparison
beats.narration: Now [cue:b4_replay]watch the same numbers flow again from inputs to output. If [cue:b4_vary]the second input grew larger, its negative contribution would pull the total down, and [cue:b4_generalize]that is the general rule: scale, add, shift, reshape.
beats.interaction: Predict: if x2 becomes 2.0, what is new output? Answer revealed as 0.1 after ReLU
beats.visual_test: Learner can write the formula from the diagram and correctly recompute output when an input value is changed

beats.cameraIntent: Static wide on left inputs and central container to establish flow order
Focus on weight arrows and product boxes, then shift to sum junction to show many-to-one convergence
Hold sum in view while revealing bias join, then pan right to activation plot and output
Static wide to keep entire chain in view during replay for comparison

answer: A single neuron computes y = activation(sum(w_i*x_i)+b). For x1=1.0, x2=0.5, w1=+0.8, w2=-0.4, b=+0.1 with ReLU: z = 0.8*1.0 + (-0.4)*0.5 + 0.1 = 0.6+0.1 = 0.7, y = ReLU(0.7)=0.7.

dslRaws.0:
beat inputs
@cue:b1_show_inputs
show neuron_body label="neuron body" zone=center_mid
show input_x1 label="1.0" zone=left_top dock=left-of:neuron_body align=top:neuron_body
show input_x2 label="0.5" zone=left_bottom dock=left-of:neuron_body align=bottom:neuron_body
@cue:b1_track_example
link flow_x1 from=input_x1 to=neuron_body style=flow
link flow_x2 from=input_x2 to=neuron_body style=flow
focus neuron_body
dslRaws.1:
beat weight_sum
retain neuron_body, input_x1, input_x2, flow_x1, flow_x2
camera frame=[input_x1, input_x2, neuron_body, product_p1, product_p2, sum_result] min_zoom=0.80
@cue:b2_show_weights
show product_p1 label="0.8" dock=right-of:input_x1
show product_p2 label="-0.2" dock=right-of:input_x2
link weight_w1 from=input_x1 to=product_p1 sign=+
link weight_w2 from=input_x2 to=product_p2 sign=-
@cue:b2_show_products
focus product_p1
focus product_p2
@cue:b2_show_sum
show sum_result label="0.8 + (-0.2) = 0.6" dock=below:product_p2
link sum_link1 from=product_p1 to=sum_result
link sum_link2 from=product_p2 to=sum_result
dslRaws.2:
beat bias_activation
retain neuron_body, input_x1, input_x2, flow_x1, flow_x2, product_p1, product_p2, weight_w1, weight_w2, sum_result, sum_link1, sum_link2
@cue:b3_add_bias
show bias_b label="bias +0.1" dock=below:sum_result
show shifted_sum label="0.7" dock=right-of:sum_result
link bias_link from=bias_b to=shifted_sum sign=+
@cue:b3_show_curve
chart activation_curve type=line data=[0:0, 0.7:0.7, 1:1] dock=right-of:shifted_sum
plot marker_dot on=activation_curve at=0.7 label="0.7"
link shift_to_act from=shifted_sum to=activation_curve
@cue:b3_show_output
show output_y label="0.7" dock=right-of:activation_curve
link act_to_out from=marker_dot to=output_y
